name: Almohad Caliphate
summary: A Berber reform movement that became a caliphate ruling North Africa and Muslim Spain. Its era produced the Giralda of Seville and philosophers such as Ibn Rushd (Averroes).

location.value: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and al-Andalus (southern Spain and Portugal).

terrain.value: The Atlas mountains, Maghreb plains and southern Iberia.
terrain.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

climate.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

resources.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

disasters.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

population.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

disease.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

migration.value: Arab tribes were moved into Morocco; Jews and Christians faced pressure to convert or leave.
migration.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

economicBase.value: Farming and Mediterranean and Saharan trade.
economicBase.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

tradeRoutes.value: Trans-Saharan gold routes and Mediterranean trade with Italian cities.
tradeRoutes.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.
wealth.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

moneyAndTax.value: The gold dinar; the Almohads introduced square silver dirhams.

inequality.value: Almohad Berber elite at the top.
inequality.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

governmentType.value: A caliphate ruled by the Mu’minid dynasty.

keyRulers.value: Ibn Tumart (Mahdi), Abd al-Mu’min (first caliph, 1130–1163), Abu Yusuf Ya‘qub al-Mansur (1184–1199).

succession.value: Hereditary in the Mu’minid family, with disputes.
succession.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

institutions.value: A strict religious hierarchy under the Mahdi’s doctrine.
institutions.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

stability.value: Weakened after Las Navas de Tolosa (1212).

eliteConflict.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

armyAndTech.value: Berber infantry and cavalry and a strong navy.
armyAndTech.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

majorWars.value: Overthrew the Almoravids (1147); won at Alarcos (1195); lost at Las Navas de Tolosa (1212).

territoryChange.value: About 2.0–2.3 million km² (1150–1200); lost Córdoba (1236) and Seville (1248).

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: Castile, Aragon, Portugal, the Almoravids.
alliancesRivals.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

inventions.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

scienceEducation.value: Philosophers Ibn Tufayl, Ibn Rushd (Averroes) and Ibn Arabi.

openness.value: Encouraged philosophy and science, but enforced strict religious doctrine.
openness.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

artsArchitecture.value: The Great Mosque of Seville and its minaret, the Giralda; the Koutoubia in Marrakesh.

socialStructure.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

sharedIdentity.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

neighbours.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

ideasReligions.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

colonisation.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

riseSignals.value: Ibn Tumart recognised as the Mahdi (c. 1121).

peakPeriod.value: Under Abu Yusuf Ya‘qub al-Mansur (1184–1199), after the victory at Alarcos (1195).
peakPeriod.source: Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

declineSignals.value: Defeat at Las Navas de Tolosa (1212) and the loss of al-Andalus.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Almohad Caliphate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)

sources.value: Arabic chronicles. Checked against Wikipedia (“Almohad Caliphate”).

knownFor.label: Giralda of Seville
knownFor.note: A minaret, now a cathedral bell tower.

knownFor.label: Ibn Rushd (Averroes)
knownFor.note: Philosopher whose commentaries on Aristotle shaped European thought.
